visualReview.reviewer: Codex reference_gate, separate from production and source authors
visualReview.scope: Actual tools.view_image inspection of 4 desktop reference pages, 4 native mobile landscape fullscreen pages, 3 mobile article-reference screenshots, and the 2 most crowded embedded mobile pages; native player controls retained.
observations: HTTP shows R1–R3 on page 1 and R4 on page 2; CDN shows R1–R3; Cookie/Session shows R1–R2. All desktop source rows, reading prompts and verification dates are visible without clipping.

All four actual native fullscreen landscape pages at 844×390 show the complete source lists with native controls retained. Fullscreen is an actual video fullscreen-element state, entered by a native button gesture.
The three mobile article screenshots show source titles, claim descriptions and full/fixed-version links wrapping inside the page; native anchor activation is measured separately.

The 390px embedded HTTP page 1 and CDN page have very small type and lower source rows affected by the native control layer. This known embedded-window limitation is retained; native fullscreen and article links provide complete reading. No body or layout rerender was requested.
limitations: Viewport-emulated Chromium; no physical phone or Safari result is claimed.
Muted playback; no new audio listening or word-level ASR was performed.
External citation navigation was prevented after native clicks; this review does not claim external source documents were fetched.
Local built-site Chromium checks; deployment identity is checked separately.
Mobile cases use Chromium viewport emulation, not a physical device or iOS Safari.
Citation links were activated with native clicks and navigation prevented; this does not claim canonical external destinations were fetched.
Playback was muted; these checks do not claim human audio listening or ASR.
390px embedded video is small and native controls can cover lower source rows; native fullscreen landscape is measured separately at 844x390.
reusedLessons: Expected chapter titles come from the immutable baseline published article; group order and starts come from its storyboard, not the production article.
Every actual reference page is inspected with native controls; small embedded mobile playback and native fullscreen are distinct observations.
Only the reference appendix changes; existing narration, dynamics and speech-listening checks are not repeated or relabeled.
